title: fleet's census walk names a bin/.devbin/lib it cannot search as a hole where installs may be missing, though nothing beneath a lib is an install
body:
## Problem

An install whose `bin/.devbin/lib` cannot be searched (its mode lost the x bit) makes the census walk say `could not read all of <root> -- installs beneath it may be missing from this scan`. Nothing beneath a vendored runtime is an install, so the line names a hole where there is none, and it points the reader at the walk rather than at the install. The census already fails on that install, correctly, through its digest (`could not digest the seam of <root>`), so the defect is the wrong message, not a wrong verdict.

0154 prunes the lib once it is marked, which removed the same false line for a directory INSIDE a lib that cannot be searched. It cannot remove it for the lib itself: `find_walk` (lib/helpers) runs its check for directories it cannot search ahead of the caller's clauses, lifting only a leading `\( ... \) -prune -o` group in front of it, so it names the lib before the lib clause in `INSTALL_MARKS` can mark and prune it. Found by critic-shell's review of 0154 v5.1 on 2026-10-05.

## Measured (cc, 2026-10-05)

A root holding one install whose lib has mode 0644, audited with `DEVBIN_FLEET_ROOTS` naming that root and `DEVBIN_FLEET_HOME` an empty directory, once on 6937d9e's code and once on 0154 v5.2. Both print the same lines, in the same order, and both exit 1:

- `devbin: cannot search <root>/est/bin/.devbin/lib -- nothing beneath it was looked at` (find_walk's own line, which is true)
- `devbin: could not read all of <root> -- installs beneath it may be missing from this scan` (fleet's line, which is not)
- `devbin: could not digest the seam of <root>/est`, and the row's digest cell reads `UNREADABLE`

So the line predates 0154, and 0154 does not change it.

## Fix

The walk must not count a lib it marks as a hole in the walk, in `find_installs` and in `outside_roots` alike, while every other directory it cannot search stays a hole. `find_walk` is shared, so either the change stays in fleet (the lib mark joins the leading prune group `find_walk` lifts ahead of its check, printing the lib there, or the two callers discount a hole that is a lib they marked), or `find_walk` gains one general way for a caller to name what it prunes, never a fleet special case.

## Done when

1. An install whose lib cannot be searched draws no `installs beneath it may be missing` line, in the roots' walk or in the walk outside the roots, and the audit still exits non-zero through the digest. Both are held by arms driven red on the base.
2. A directory that is not a lib and cannot be searched is still named as a hole, and still fails the audit, held by the existing arms.
3. It ships in the 0.1.9 bundle.

## Resolution

Fixed at eb9166e1. fleet's census walk marks a vendored lib in the walk's own prune group, which find_walk asks before its check for a directory it can list but not search. So an install whose bin/.devbin/lib has lost its x bit is printed, pruned and never named a hole. `install_walk` is the one walk for installs, shared by the walk under the roots and the walk outside them, and find_walk is unchanged. The mark goes by its exact path, so every other directory the walk cannot search is still a hole, a project's own lib/ and a .devbin/lib outside bin/ among them.

Against the done-when list:

1. Under the roots, an install whose lib cannot be searched draws no "installs beneath it may be missing" line, and the audit still exits non-zero, through its digest, which names the seam it could not digest. Outside the roots the audit now passes, where this issue promised non-zero in both walks. That walk digests nothing, so its only failure here was the false hole, and its question, which installs exist outside the roots, is answered in full: the install is listed. Both arms are red on the base, at the hole line. And a sweep is no longer refused whole for one such estate: it is planned, and `--apply` names it FAILED when its own launcher cannot run, while the rest are swept.
2. A directory that is not a lib and cannot be searched is still named as a hole and still fails the audit: the existing arms at modes 000 and 0644, under the roots and outside them, pass unchanged, and a new arm holds the same for lib-shaped directories that are not bin/.devbin/lib.
3. It ships in the 0.1.9 bundle.

Evidence. 8 mutants over fleet, all killed, two of them the looser lib paths critic-shell found surviving the first version. fleet.bats runs green under GNU findutils as well as BSD find. The full suite on the landing tree: 2106 of 2106 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261005-1255), 12:55:44Z to 13:46:16Z, on main with 0173, 0169 and 0166 landed and 0175 above this change; 5 skipped, each as expected.
